title: Spendora - Conversational AI for Expense Insights
summary: I built an LLM-powered conversational AI assistant that provides personalized expense insights using retrieval-augmented generation and tool-based reasoning.

problem.whatProblem: How can users get intelligent insights about their spending habits through natural conversation?
problem.whoForIsWas: Anyone wanting AI-powered financial analysis without manual data analysis
problem.whyDidItMatter: Most expense tracking tools lack conversational intelligence and context-aware recommendations

context.constraints: Limited time, focus on LLM integration quality

architecture.backend: LangChain conversational agents with memory management
architecture.dataModelStorage: Custom financial data toolchains, vector embeddings for RAG
architecture.outputUserExperience: Conversational interface with context-aware financial recommendations

technicalDecisions.whyIChoseIt: Simplifies memory management and tool-use patterns for conversational AI
Enables grounding in actual financial data without fine-tuning

tradeoffs: RAG adds latency for retrieval but improves accuracy over hallucination-prone base models
Multiple toolchains provide flexibility but increase complexity

title: News Headline Classification
summary: I built an LSTM-based deep learning model that classifies news headlines with 93.28% accuracy on a dataset of 400K+ headlines.

problem.whatProblem: Automatically categorize news headlines into topics for content organization
problem.whyDidItMatter: Manual classification is time-consuming; automated systems improve discoverability

architecture.backend: LSTM neural network with embedding layers
architecture.dataModelStorage: spaCy for preprocessing, PyTorch for training
architecture.outputUserExperience: Predicted category labels with confidence scores

technicalDecisions.decision: Used LSTM over simpler models like logistic regression
technicalDecisions.whyIChoseIt: Captures sequential dependencies in text better than bag-of-words approaches
technicalDecisions.alternativeConsidered: Transformer-based models, but LSTM was more interpretable

tradeoffs: LSTM training is slower than simpler models but provides better accuracy
Model requires GPU for practical training time

metrics.whatItMeasured: Correct classification rate on test set
Speed of preprocessing and training pipeline

title: Media Recommendation System
summary: I developed a personalized recommendation system for movies, music, and books using multiple algorithms including collaborative filtering, content-based filtering, and clustering.

problem.whatProblem: Help users discover relevant media across different content types
problem.whyDidItMatter: Personalization drives engagement and user satisfaction

architecture.input: User ratings, viewing/listening history, item metadata
architecture.backend: Multiple recommendation algorithms working in ensemble
architecture.dataModelStorage: Flask backend, React frontend, Spotify API integration
architecture.outputUserExperience: Ranked recommendations across movies, music, and books

technicalDecisions.decision: Implemented multiple algorithms: Cosine Similarity for content-based filtering, Pearson Correlation for collaborative filtering, K-Nearest Neighbors (KNN) for user-based recommendations, K-Means Clustering for user segmentation, and TF-IDF for content analysis and feature extraction
technicalDecisions.whyIChoseIt: Different algorithms capture different recommendation signals
Combines strengths of multiple methods for better recommendations

tradeoffs: Ensemble approach harder to explain than single algorithm

metrics.whatItMeasured: System successfully used content-based, collaborative, K-means, TF-IDF

whatIWouldImproveNext: Implement deep learning models (neural collaborative filtering)

title: SoundScape - Android Music Streaming App
summary: I built an end-to-end Android music streaming app with API integration and intelligent caching that reduced API calls by 70%.

problem.whatProblem: Create a functional music streaming experience on Android
problem.whyDidItMatter: Demonstrates full-stack mobile development and real-world performance optimization

context.constraints: Android platform limitations, API rate limits

architecture.backend: Android SDK with REST API integration
architecture.dataModelStorage: Room database for caching, MediaPlayer for playback
architecture.outputUserExperience: Music streaming player with search, playlist, and playback controls

technicalDecisions.decision: Implemented Room caching layer for Musixmatch API responses
technicalDecisions.whyIChoseIt: Reduces API calls by 70% and improves user experience with instant data
technicalDecisions.alternativeConsidered: No caching, direct API calls (slower, hits rate limits)

technicalDecisions.whyIChoseIt: Separates concerns, makes each component independently testable

tradeoffs: Caching adds storage requirements but dramatically improves performance
Microservices add complexity but improve maintainability

metrics.whatItMeasured: Fewer requests to Musixmatch due to caching

metrics.exactMetric: Full music streaming feature set implemented

whatIWouldImproveNext: Support additional music sources beyond Musixmatch

title: PolicyPilot - Medical Benefit Policy Intelligence Portal
summary: I built a citation-backed RAG portal that unifies fragmented multi-payer insurance policies so clinicians can answer drug coverage and prior-authorization questions without digging through 50-500 page PDFs.

problem.whatProblem: Clinicians manually dig through 50-500 page insurance payer policy PDFs to answer drug coverage/prior-authorization eligibility questions
problem.whoForIsWas: Clinicians and care teams handling prior-authorization and coverage eligibility decisions
problem.whyDidItMatter: Fragmented, unversioned payer policy data makes it easy to silently surface criteria from an outdated policy in a high-stakes healthcare decision

context.constraints: Hackathon timeframe; healthcare data required citation-backed accuracy over speed

architecture.input: Multi-payer policy PDFs and patient documents
architecture.backend: Express 5 REST API + 17-tool MCP server on a single Node.js process
architecture.dataModelStorage: PDF-to-structured-data pipeline (parse -> clean -> chunk -> validate) with Zod schema validation at data boundaries
architecture.outputUserExperience: React SPA with unified drug coverage search across payers, cross-payer side-by-side comparison, real-time policy-change tracking, AI chat for coverage/PA/eligibility questions, and an Evidence Explorer for verifying answers against source documents

technicalDecisions.decision: Architected an evidence-grounded RAG pipeline forcing citation-backed answers
technicalDecisions.whyIChoseIt: Eliminates hallucination risk in high-stakes healthcare eligibility decisions
technicalDecisions.alternativeConsidered: Unconstrained LLM chat responses without mandatory citations

technicalDecisions.decision: Designed a 17-tool MCP server (e.g. get_drug_coverage, check_patient_readiness, diff_policy_versions) exposing structured LLM tool-calling for PA extraction, patient-readiness evaluation, and cross-payer comparison
technicalDecisions.whyIChoseIt: Lets external AI agents replace manual multi-payer PDF lookups with direct queries
technicalDecisions.alternativeConsidered: A single monolithic chat endpoint without discrete tool boundaries

technicalDecisions.decision: Migrated from Ollama to Gemini 2.5-flash after benchmarking
technicalDecisions.whyIChoseIt: Lower hallucination rates on policy-grounded questions
technicalDecisions.alternativeConsidered: Staying on Ollama for local/self-hosted inference

technicalDecisions.decision: Built citation/version tracing into every LLM answer
technicalDecisions.whyIChoseIt: Surfaces retrieval mismatches (e.g. an outdated policy version) immediately instead of silently misleading a provider

tradeoffs: Citation-backed grounding adds retrieval and validation overhead but is required for healthcare-safe answers
Retrieval and document structure mattered more than the model choice - policy PDFs vary widely in layout, and the same rule can appear under different sections, headings, or tables
Standards like HL7's Da Vinci FHIR guides only cover transmitting coverage details - keeping underlying multi-payer data correct and versioned was the harder problem

metrics.exactMetric: 17 MCP tool APIs with Zod validation at every data boundary
metrics.whatItMeasured: Eliminated a class of runtime type-mismatch bugs across all external tool calls
axe-core accessibility test coverage on the PDF-to-structured-data pipeline

whatIWouldImproveNext: Expand payer coverage beyond the initial dataset

title: NYC Mobility Forecasting - ML-Driven Taxi/Rideshare Demand Prediction System
summary: I built an end-to-end ML system forecasting NYC taxi/rideshare demand across 263 zones, cutting prediction error (RMSE) by 43% over a baseline Random Forest and serving live predictions through a REST API and dashboard.

problem.whatProblem: Forecast NYC taxi/FHV demand at zone/hour granularity to support supply planning and surge-risk awareness
problem.whoForIsWas: Rideshare/taxi operations planning and demand-forecasting use cases
problem.whyDidItMatter: Accurate zone/hour demand forecasts reduce both undersupply and oversupply risk in a highly variable transportation market

context.constraints: Large-scale data processing (2.3M-row hourly dataset); free-tier cloud deployment budget

architecture.input: NYC TLC trip data, weather data, geospatial zone data
architecture.backend: Spark-based medallion (bronze/silver/gold) pipeline; two-stage classification + regression Poisson hurdle model
architecture.dataModelStorage: PySpark, Delta Lake, PostgreSQL, Redis caching
architecture.outputUserExperience: React/map-based dashboard consuming a FastAPI REST API for real-time demand predictions

technicalDecisions.decision: Used a two-stage (classification + regression) Poisson hurdle model instead of a single regression model
technicalDecisions.whyIChoseIt: Better captures the zero-inflated nature of hourly zone-level demand (many zone/hours have zero trips) than a plain regression baseline
Processes trip and weather data into a clean 2.3M-row hourly demand dataset at scale with reproducible stages

technicalDecisions.decision: Targeted free-tier Oracle Cloud for deployment
technicalDecisions.whyIChoseIt: Keeps the project runnable end-to-end without ongoing cloud spend

tradeoffs: Two-stage model adds pipeline complexity over a single regressor but meaningfully improves accuracy on sparse-demand zones
Free-tier cloud deployment constrains available compute/memory for serving

metrics.whatItMeasured: Forecast accuracy vs baseline Random Forest

metrics.exactMetric: RMSE cut by 43%, MAE cut by 53%
metrics.whatItMeasured: Prediction error vs baseline Random Forest
Scale of forecasting system and processed dataset

whatIWouldImproveNext: Add real-time streaming ingestion instead of batch pipeline

title: Spotify Personal Analytics Platform - Full-Stack Data Analytics App
summary: I built a personal analytics platform that processes a 71K+ event Spotify streaming-history export through a 4-stage Python ETL pipeline and serves insights via a FastAPI backend and React/MUI dashboard.

problem.whatProblem: Turn a raw Spotify GDPR streaming-history export into queryable, enriched personal listening analytics
problem.whoForIsWas: Personal use - anyone wanting deeper insight into their own Spotify listening history than the built-in Spotify Wrapped/stats provide
problem.whyDidItMatter: Raw GDPR exports are unenriched JSON with no genre/lyrics context and no queryable interface

context.constraints: Spotify API rate limits; multi-source lyrics API reliability

architecture.backend: 4-stage Python ETL pipeline (dedup/extraction -> metadata + genre enrichment -> two-stage lyrics ingestion -> validation) + FastAPI backend
architecture.dataModelStorage: PostgreSQL (Supabase) analytics schema with materialized views, composite/partial indexes, 16 SQL RPC functions
architecture.externalAPIs: Spotify Web API (spotipy), Genius API (lyricsgenius), musixmatch-api
architecture.outputUserExperience: React/MUI dashboard with charts (MUI X Charts) over pre-aggregated analytics queries

technicalDecisions.decision: Built a 4-stage ETL pipeline with custom rate limiting and exponential-backoff retry handling
technicalDecisions.whyIChoseIt: Spotify Web API enrichment for 71K+ events needed resilient handling of rate limits without dropping data
technicalDecisions.alternativeConsidered: Naive sequential API calls without backoff

technicalDecisions.decision: Built a genre-enrichment pipeline by joining artist-level metadata
technicalDecisions.whyIChoseIt: Spotify's API doesn't expose track-level genre directly, so joining via artist metadata was needed to enrich 13K+ tracks

technicalDecisions.decision: Two-stage lyrics ingestion (batch + retry) with checkpointing and multi-source API fallback
technicalDecisions.whyIChoseIt: Processing 13.8K tracks against lyrics APIs needed resilience to per-source failures and the ability to resume from checkpoints, with automatic failure-based source disabling

technicalDecisions.decision: Designed a PostgreSQL analytics schema with materialized views and 16 SQL RPC functions
technicalDecisions.whyIChoseIt: Enables low-latency pre-aggregated queries over streaming history instead of computing aggregates at request time
technicalDecisions.alternativeConsidered: Computing all aggregates on-demand in the API layer

tradeoffs: Materialized views add refresh/maintenance overhead but keep dashboard queries fast
Multi-source lyrics fallback increases pipeline complexity but improves coverage across 13.8K tracks

metrics.exactMetric: 13.8K tracks processed via two-stage lyrics ingestion
16 SQL RPC functions over a materialized-view analytics schema
metrics.whatItMeasured: Query layer supporting low-latency pre-aggregated analytics
